docRequirement: best-practices.md line 482 binds the shape of our non-interactive output: "The `stream-json` format prints one JSON object per line, starting with an init event." So `--output-format stream-json` must emit newline-delimited JSON AND the stream's first object must be an init event. headless.md:197 spells that frame `system/init` ("The `system/init` event reports session metadata including the model, tools, MCP servers, and loaded plugins. It is the first event in the stream unless startup events precede it"). The same best-practices sentence also binds `json`: "The `json` format returns a single JSON object with a `result` field."
current: `--output-format stream-json` is real and does emit one JSON object per line, but each line is a verbatim server event and there is no leading frame. `apps/cli/src/index.ts:457` sets `const streamJson = args.outputFormat === 'stream-json'`; inside the `client.on('session:event', ...)` subscription the only stream-json write is `process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(ev) + '\n')` at `apps/cli/src/index.ts:469-471` — a passthrough of the server's `session:event` payload (`text_delta`, `text_complete`, `tool_start`, `tool_result`, `error`, `typed_error`, `complete`, `interrupted`, and the types the text renderer ignores). Nothing is written to stdout before the send at `apps/cli/src/index.ts:548-552`: both callers reach it with no prior stdout write (`cmdSend` at `apps/cli/src/index.ts:591`, `cmdRun` at `apps/cli/src/index.ts:852`), the run path's pre-turn output goes to stderr (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:838` `Project selected: …`, plus `Starting server...`), and the spawned server's own stdout is piped and consumed by the spawner rather than inherited (`apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:71`, `:127-145`), so the first stdout line a consumer sees is whichever session event arrives first. No init/system member exists in either event union: `SessionEvent` (`packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:343-395`) and `AgentEvent` (`packages/core/src/types/message.ts:966-1014`). The repo touches `system/init` only on the READER side — the Claude backend's adapter consumes the SDK's init at `packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:625-630`, stashes `msg.tools` in `this._sdkTools` and emits no `AgentEvent`, so even the metadata we already receive is dropped before it can reach the stream. Our keys are camelCase (`sessionId`), not Claude's `session_id`. Our own reference docs describe exactly today's shape: `docs-site/content/reference/cli.md:150` and `docs-site/content/ru/reference/cli.md:146` ("every session event is written to stdout as one JSON object per line … Nothing else is printed"). The `json` half of the sentence is also unmet: `structuredMode` requires a schema (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:463` `const structuredMode = outputSchema !== undefined && !streamJson`), so `--output-format json` without `--json-schema` falls through to the plain-text renderer and prints no `{ "result": … }` object.
divergence: The per-line-JSON half of the sentence is satisfied; the mandated FIRST object is absent entirely. This is not a key-name mismatch and not a wrong value — no object of any spelling (`system`, `init`, `subtype`) is written before the first server event, in either `run` or `send`. Two things narrow the delta and change the fix: (a) the frame can be produced purely in the CLI, because best-practices.md binds only its existence and position, while the field-level contract (`tools`, `plugins`, `plugin_errors`, `mcp_servers`, `mcp_server_errors`, `capabilities`) lives on headless.md and is the separate f180/f133 scope; (b) our subsequent lines are camelCase Nessy `session:event` objects, so adding a Claude-spelled snake_case init frame makes the stream Claude-shaped in its first line only — the casing convention must be a deliberate, documented choice, not an accident. Adjacent, from the same doc sentence and therefore worth naming here: `--output-format json` returns a `result`-bearing object only when `--json-schema` rides the run, and even then the payload is `.structured_output`, not `result`.

change.what: Emit the init frame once, when `streamJson`, AFTER the `client.on('session:event', …)` subscription is installed (so no event can be lost) and BEFORE the `client.invoke('sessions:sendMessage', …)` at :548-552: `process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ type: 'system', subtype: 'init', session_id: sessionId, cwd: args.workspaceDir ?? process.cwd(), model: args.model, permissionMode: args.mode ? parsePermissionMode(args.mode) ?? args.mode : undefined, sources: args.sources, output_format: 'stream-json' }) + '\n')`. Every field is already in scope — no new RPC and no signature change. Never emit in text or structured mode (the `!streamJson` guards at :476, :488, :491, :502, :512, :533, :539 are the existing pattern). Pick and comment ONE casing convention for the frame (Claude's snake_case, matching the doc, vs our camelCase events) — the mixed stream is the trap here. Optional, only if the live model is wanted when `--model` is omitted: thread `workspaceId` into `sendAndStream` and read `session:getModel(sessionId, workspaceId)` (handler `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/settings.ts:167`, returns `string | null`, already allowlisted at `settings.ts:46`) best-effort with `.catch(() => null)`.

One test: in stream-json mode the FIRST stdout line parses as JSON and is `type: 'system'` / `subtype: 'init'` carrying the session id — spy on `process.stdout.write` and assert on line 1, and assert the second line is the first session event. The existing mock server needs no change: unknown channels resolve to `null` via `default: result = null` at `apps/cli/src/run.test.ts:143`. The existing stream-json cases (`:316`, `:349`) assert exit codes only and stay green.

Replace "Nothing else is printed" with the new shape: the stream starts with a `system`/`init` frame carrying session metadata, then one session event per line; exit-code behavior unchanged. One line.

Same one-line edit in the Russian mirror; the two pages must move in the same commit. `docs/cli.md:165` and the CLI help text at `apps/cli/src/index.ts:2048` only list the format names and need no change.

Adjacent and explicitly NOT folded into the init-frame fix: `--output-format json` without `--json-schema` currently prints prose because `structuredMode` requires a schema (:463). The doc-bound shape is a single JSON object with a `result` field, assembled at the `complete` arm (:517-535). Fix it with f180 (which owns the result frame and its cost/usage fields) rather than here, or as a deliberate small addition — do not silently rely on the init frame closing it.

blastRadius: The CLI-only fix touches no wire and no persistence boundary — `SessionEvent` (`packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:343`) and `AgentEvent` (`packages/core/src/types/message.ts:966`) are untouched, so it is not a risk trigger. Readers of the changed function: two production callers, `cmdSend` (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:591`) and `cmdRun` (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:852`); `sendAndStream` is exported and driven directly by `apps/cli/src/run.test.ts:341`, `:375`, `:412`, `:563`. The only in-repo consumer of the stream is `scripts/test-workflow-local.sh:22`, which just prints it, so an extra first line breaks nothing there — but it IS an output-contract change for any external CI job parsing line 1 of our stream today, which is the reason to land it with the docs edit. Docs that assert the current shape and must move together: `docs-site/content/reference/cli.md:150`, `docs-site/content/ru/reference/cli.md:146`. If instead the frame is made server-side to carry the documented `tools`/`plugins`/`mcp_servers` fields (f180/f133), that DOES cross the wire boundary: a new member in both `SessionEvent` and `AgentEvent`, every renderer `session:event` consumer (`apps/electron/src/renderer/event-processor/*`), and the channel test `apps/electron/src/shared/__tests__/ipc-channels.test.ts` — a risk trigger under the repo's verification budget. A middle path that stays CLI-side is reading `capabilities:getCatalog` (`packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/capabilities.ts:133`, session-scoped and requires `ctx.workspaceId` to match) for plugin/MCP names.
userImpact: A CI job or script that runs `nessy-general-agent run --output-format stream-json "…"` (or `send`) and was written against Claude Code's stream-json contract reads nothing at line 1: `jq -s '.[0] | select(.type=="system" and .subtype=="init")'` yields empty, because the first line is a raw event such as `{"type":"text_delta","sessionId":"…","delta":"…"}` (or `status`/`info`/`usage_update`, whichever the server sends first). Anything that gate reads from the init frame — the model actually used, `session_id`, the tool list, and per f180/f133 whether a plugin or MCP server failed to load — is unavailable, so the gate either errors or silently passes on an empty match. Same command with `--output-format json` and no `--json-schema` prints prose, so `| jq .result` fails too. Interactive desktop users: none observable — this is the headless surface only, and it would surface for them only if a Nessy stream were fed to a Claude-Code-oriented tool.
